AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #1 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. About how high should a compost heap be built? (1 mark)
   A. About as high as your chest
   B. As flat as the ground
   C. As high as a house
   D. Only one hand high

2. Where is the best place to make a compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. In the middle of a stream
   B. In a very windy open road
   C. A shady, well-drained place near the garden
   D. Inside the kitchen

3. Which waste should NOT be put in a compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. Chicken droppings
   B. Plastic bags
   C. Fresh grass
   D. Banana peelings

4. Why do we cover a compost heap? (1 mark)
   A. To make it heavier
   B. To hide it from animals only
   C. To stop it from rotting
   D. To keep off rain and sun

5. What is the best time of day to water crops? (1 mark)
   A. Midnight only
   B. Noon
   C. Never
   D. Early morning or late afternoon

6. Which is a benefit of drip irrigation? (1 mark)
   A. More weeds grow
   B. The leaves get very wet
   C. Fewer weeds grow between plants
   D. Water is wasted

7. Why does a higher container give a faster drip? (1 mark)
   A. It is nearer the sun
   B. It has a lid
   C. It has more air
   D. Gravity pushes the water more strongly

8. Why should the end of the drip pipe be closed? (1 mark)
   A. So water does not run out of the end
   B. So the pipe looks nice
   C. So rainwater cannot enter
   D. So the plants do not drink

9. Which stove saves more charcoal? (1 mark)
   A. An improved jiko
   B. An open fire in the wind
   C. A broken pot
   D. A stone on the ground

10. What is the danger of burning charcoal in a closed room? (1 mark)
   A. It makes the room too cold
   B. It makes the walls bigger
   C. It gives off a poisonous gas
   D. It creates rain

11. Why is wet firewood a poor fuel? (1 mark)
   A. It burns very hot
   B. It makes a lot of smoke and gives little heat
   C. It has no smoke
   D. It lasts forever

12. Which action wastes fuel? (1 mark)
   A. Turning the flame down after boiling starts
   B. Using a lid
   C. Boiling water with no lid and a big flame
   D. Using dry wood

13. Which crop is likely to be eaten by birds? (1 mark)
   A. Compost
   B. Firewood
   C. Ripening millet
   D. Rocks

14. What is a scarecrow? (1 mark)
   A. A figure made to look like a person to scare animals
   B. A wild bird
   C. A kind of fence
   D. A farm tool for digging

15. Which tool should an adult use to help fix the scarecrow pole? (1 mark)
   A. A bare hand only
   B. A tin of paint
   C. A hammer or heavy stone to push it in
   D. A knife on the pole

16. Why is it wrong to kill every bird that visits a field? (1 mark)
   A. Birds also eat harmful insects and are part of nature
   B. Birds pay tax
   C. Birds cannot eat crops
   D. Birds are always good

17. Why should a seedbed for tiny seeds be fine? (1 mark)
   A. It is a school rule
   B. Lumps help seeds
   C. Tiny seeds cannot push through big lumps
   D. Fine soil makes seeds bigger

18. Why are weeds removed from the seedbed? (1 mark)
   A. They take water, light and food from the crop
   B. They add manure
   C. They are colourful
   D. They protect seedlings from rain

19. Why do we cover the seeds with a thin layer of fine soil? (1 mark)
   A. To make them bigger
   B. To protect them and keep them moist
   C. To stop them growing
   D. To let birds find them

20. What is direct sowing? (1 mark)
   A. Sowing seeds where the crop will grow until harvest
   B. Sowing in a nursery
   C. Buying young plants
   D. Watering seeds

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Write the steps for growing carrots from seed to harvest. (5 marks)

22. Sila has a millet field where birds eat the grain every morning. Suggest and explain a plan to protect the crop without killing the birds. (5 marks)

23. Give three ways of caring for a drip irrigation system. (3 marks)

24. Why should kerosene never be poured onto a fire? (2 marks)

25. Name three small wild animals that destroy crops. (3 marks)

26. Why is poison or a trap not a good way of dealing with wild animals? (4 marks)

27. Describe how to care for a seedbed after sowing. (4 marks)

28. Explain why we must not leave a fire burning after cooking. (2 marks)

29. Explain what drip irrigation is. (2 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — TERMLY EXAM #1 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. A — About as high as your chest
   A heap that is too low loses heat and one that is too high is hard to turn.

2. C — A shady, well-drained place near the garden
   A shaded, dry spot protects the heap from sun and flooding.

3. B — Plastic bags
   Plastic does not rot and spoils the compost.

4. D — To keep off rain and sun
   A cover protects the heap from too much rain and drying sun.

5. D — Early morning or late afternoon
   The sun is less hot, so less water evaporates.

6. C — Fewer weeds grow between plants
   The soil between plants stays dry so fewer weeds grow.

7. D — Gravity pushes the water more strongly
   A higher container gives a bigger push for water flowing down.

8. A — So water does not run out of the end
   An open end would waste water.

9. A — An improved jiko
   An improved jiko holds heat around the pot.

10. C — It gives off a poisonous gas
   Charcoal fumes can make people ill or worse.

11. B — It makes a lot of smoke and gives little heat
   Wet wood wastes heat drying itself.

12. C — Boiling water with no lid and a big flame
   Heat escapes without a lid and a big flame.

13. C — Ripening millet
   Birds eat ripening grain such as millet and sorghum.

14. A — A figure made to look like a person to scare animals
   A scarecrow frightens away birds and other animals.

15. C — A hammer or heavy stone to push it in
   An adult helps with heavy or sharp work.

16. A — Birds also eat harmful insects and are part of nature
   Wild animals are needed for balance in nature.

17. C — Tiny seeds cannot push through big lumps
   Tiny seeds have little food and are weak.

18. A — They take water, light and food from the crop
   Weeds compete with crops.

19. B — To protect them and keep them moist
   Covering helps seeds germinate.

20. A — Sowing seeds where the crop will grow until harvest
   The seedlings are never moved.

SECTION B
----
21. (5 marks)
   Answer: Prepare a fine seedbed; make drills about 1 cm deep; sow seeds thinly with sand; cover and water gently; thin to about 5 cm; weed and water; harvest after three to four months by loosening the soil and pulling.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct stage, up to 5.

22. (5 marks)
   Answer: Make a scarecrow with tins and shiny strips, place it in the field, move it every few days, and use a net or a noise maker. Avoid poison because it harms other living things.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for scarecrow and moving it, 1 mark for another method, 1 mark for avoiding poison, 1 mark for reason.

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: Fill the container daily, check for leaks and blocked holes, keep the water covered and clean.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

24. (2 marks)
   Answer: It catches fire quickly and can burst into flames and burn people.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for catching fire, 1 mark for danger.

25. (3 marks)
   Answer: Birds, hares, squirrels, monkeys (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct animal.

26. (4 marks)
   Answer: It can kill other animals, pets and people, it hurts animals, and it harms nature.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct reason, up to 4.

27. (4 marks)
   Answer: Water gently and regularly, remove weeds, thin the seedlings, and protect the bed from animals and birds.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct activity.

28. (2 marks)
   Answer: It wastes fuel and can cause a fire or accident.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for waste, 1 mark for danger.

29. (2 marks)
   Answer: It is watering plants slowly, drop by drop, next to their roots.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for slowly or drop by drop, 1 mark for near the roots.
